Dumelang ditsala! Re a lo amogela. Pula!
Hello friends! Welcome. Pula!

How to use the app

African Wildlife Survey: field guide, records, surveys and learning

The app is a field guide to 466 species of birds, mammals, reptiles and insects in Botswana, and a tool for recording what you see and hear. Everything works without internet or mobile signal.

The lists

  • The tabs at the bottom are Birds, Mammals, Reptiles, Insects, Map and Records.
  • Tap + on a card each time you see that species. The app saves the date, time, area and GPS spot.
  • The small minus button takes one back.
  • Use the chips to sort the list or show only what you have not recorded yet.
  • The button at the top right shows your area. GPS changes it as you move.

A species page

  • Tap a card to open its page. Swipe the photos sideways.
  • + adds a record. + Heard adds one you only heard.
  • Add an earlier sighting lets you set the date, time, place and number for something you saw before.
  • Google Maps opens the places where you recorded it.

Learning about a species

  • Scroll down for how to identify it, size, behaviour, key notes, group names and where to look.
  • Many birds have a Call you can play. Please do not play calls to attract birds.
  • Your sighting log and notes are at the bottom. Tap a log line to change it.
  • A shield marks sensitive species. Their exact spots are hidden when you share or export.

Search

  • Tap Search at the top and type any word: a name, a colour, a habit or a place.
  • It searches every word of every species. Try red bill or long tail when you do not know the name.
  • Tap + to record straight from the results.

Starting a survey

  • A survey is a timed count at one site.
  • Go to Records and tap Start a survey.
  • Enter the site name, the observers and any weather notes.
  • The atlas pentad (the bird atlas square) is worked out from GPS.
  • Tap Start survey.

Recording during a survey

  • Type part of a name, then tap + Seen, or the ear button if you only heard it.
  • You can also tap + on any list while the survey is running. A green bar shows that a survey is open.
  • Each species appears once in the survey. Tapping again adds to its count.

Counts, and ending the survey

  • Use + and the minus button beside each species to set how many you counted.
  • Tap Seen to switch it to Heard, and back.
  • When you finish, tap End survey.

Sharing a survey

  • Share report sends a text report by WhatsApp, email or any app.
  • Export survey CSV makes a spreadsheet file for the club's records.
  • Past surveys stay listed under Records.

Monthly report

  • In Records, tap Monthly report and choose the month.
  • Share my report sends your own summary.
  • Send my month file to the club makes a small file with your records for the month. It has areas but no GPS positions.
  • Club report: the person who puts it together taps Add a member's file for each member, then Share club report. Do this in one sitting, as members' files are not kept after the app closes.

Quiz

  • In Records, tap Quiz.
  • Name the animal from its photo, or choose Call to name a bird from its sound (needs the bird calls pack).
  • Good for club meetings and school visits.

Map

  • Every record with GPS is a dot on the satellite map, which works without internet.
  • Filter by group or by date. Tap a dot, or use Previous and Next.
  • Open in Google Maps shows that spot in Google Maps.

Records

  • See how many species you have recorded in each group, what you logged today, and your new species by date.
  • Share and export has the picture card for Facebook or WhatsApp and the map file (KML) for Google My Maps.

Settings

  • Your name is used on surveys and exports.
  • Language: English or Setswana.
  • List order and Current area.
  • GPS tagging: turn off to save battery. Records then keep only the area.
  • Sensitive species: keep this on, so exact spots of birds such as vultures, cranes and Pel's Fishing Owl stay hidden in shared files.

Backup

  • Backup file saves all your records to one file. Send it to yourself every week or two.
  • Restore from backup puts a backup onto a new phone.
  • Export CSV makes a spreadsheet of every record.
  • Clear all sightings deletes everything. Make a backup first.
  • Night mode dims the screen for night work.

The Setswana in the app and guides was drafted with computer help. If you see a mistake, please email apps@warrimoo.net.
